deck: Korea’s entrance exams open · Homebirth rallies across Australia · IRGC claims a Hormuz drone intercept

leads.headline: Essay and interview exams begin this weekend
leads.detail: Fourteen universities hold essay exams, among them Konkuk, Kyung Hee, Korea and Sogang (natural sciences), Sungkyunkwan (language), Sookmyung and Soongsil. Yonsei and Ewha start interviews on the 21st.

leads.headline: Rallies warn homebirth access may collapse
leads.detail: Dozens of rallies in cities and towns say new insurance rules will bring a “catastrophic collapse” in midwife-supported homebirth access, and that freebirths will soar.

leads.headline: IRGC says it shot down a US MQ-9 drone
leads.detail: Iran’s IRGC says the drone fell over the Strait of Hormuz and calls it the 58th it has downed. The report is a claim, not a confirmed US loss.

features.headline: Board backs Cummins as captain
features.detail: Cricket Australia’s board is unanimous while the sandpaper controversy continues.

features.headline: Teens stabbed at a shopping centre
features.detail: Two boys were stabbed and a 17-year-old was charged. Police say they were lucky to be alive.

features.headline: Lightning strikes four at a festival
features.detail: It happened at Strawberry Fields, Tocumwal, NSW, after wild weather overnight.

features.headline: Boy, 11, killed on a highway
features.detail: A ute hit him as he crossed South Western Highway in Kirup, south of Perth.

features.headline: Schoolies begins; numbers are down
features.detail: Thousands of leavers arrive. Organisers add pickleball and line dancing.

features.headline: Ministry weighs blocking extortion sites
features.detail: After a GMO access case, critics say ISP cut-offs may breach secrecy of communications.

features.headline: Tashima stays in the FIFA race
features.detail: He is a March candidate with the incumbent and the French FA president, and he is not withdrawing.

features.headline: Petition opposes junior AI cameras
features.detail: The petition targets a Basketball Australia trial of smart cameras.

features.headline: Party seeks orders on IEBC chief
features.detail: It wants a court to stop the appointment of the electoral commission’s CEO.

features.headline: Report: nearly 600 women killed
features.detail: Premium Times published a three-month total on Saturday, not a single-day toll.

briefs.line: Gohar seeks fair treatment for detained PTI workers, their security, and reserved seats.
A phone explodes on an e-bus; passengers smash glass; some minor injuries.
Dirty foam on the Ngwempisi River sparks a pollution probe.
Authorities probe a four-minute Triple Zero outage and a failed power backup.
Staff covered ¥54m in unpaid school fees; about ¥37m is due back to the principal.
Mills get wheat at Rs4,500 per 40kg; a 10kg flour bag is to retail at Rs1,275.
Saturday report: Pakistan up 17 e-government places, to High; telecoms score 0.6590.
Gujranwala and Multan pass Lahore on air pollution; four other cities are high.
A magistrate indicts anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan for cyberterrorism.
The assembly takes up rising dog bites; Sharjeel says hospital staff lack protocols.
SECP will take filings only when the auditor’s report has a valid UDIN.
Peter Obi vows to end kidnappings and corruption.
The ECC lowers the SME export threshold and approves supplementary grants.
The assembly wants Quetta–Sukkur flights and votes on officers, TV offices and media jobs.
Digital monitoring is ordered for paper and rexine plants, not firms that only cut and print.
A secret police recording of Raelene Polymiadis is released.
